reviews.title: ⭐ 1/5 — Coffee Meets Paywall!
reviews.text:
Absolutely ridiculous! Coffee Meets Bagel has turned dating into a never-ending paywall. You get a whopping 15 swipes every 24 hours, and practically everything else comes with a price tag. Want more options? Pay. Want more freedom to explore? Pay. Want to actually enjoy the app without constant restrictions? Good luck!

What’s the point of a dating app that limits your choices so aggressively and then expects you to pay just to have a decent experience?

At this point, it feels less like a platform designed to help people find meaningful connections and more like a subscription business designed to squeeze money out of users.

It’s called Coffee Meets Bagel, but apparently, the only real match they’re interested in is your credit card.

reviews.title: Disappointing Experience After Six Months of Premium Membership
reviews.text:
After paying for the most expensive subscription and using the app for six months, I was extremely disappointed. Instead of meeting new people, I kept seeing the same 10 or so profiles circulating over and over again. The same people would repeatedly send likes and hearts, even after I had already X’d them out. They just kept coming back!
There should be an option to permanently block or remove profiles you’re not interested in so they don’t keep appearing in your searches.
I also encountered numerous suspicious profiles that appeared to be AI-generated or operated by scammers. At times, I even wondered whether some of these fake profiles were being used to keep subscribers engaged and paying. I have no proof of that, but the experience certainly raised questions.
Another feature I strongly disliked was the tracking of who initiates conversations, who responds, and how quickly people reply. Dating should feel natural, not like a performance evaluation.
After six months of paying for a premium membership, I felt like I was browsing the same handful of people repeatedly, with very little opportunity to meet anyone new.
Expensive, repetitive, and ultimately a waste of my time and money.

reviews.title: Being advertised as one of the best dating apps, yet having one of the worst filtering systems.
reviews.text:
When creating a profile, one of the prompts asks, “Who do you want to date?” with the options being Women, Men, or Everyone. I selected Men. However, after a few months of using the app, I noticed that my daily suggestions progressively started showing me more women than men. At this point, the majority of my suggestions are women, despite clearly indicating that I’m only interested in dating men. What makes this even more frustrating is that you can’t simply keep swiping or refresh your suggestions, you have to wait until the next refresh. This makes the issue even more noticeable because a significant portion of the limited suggestions I receive aren’t even people I’m interested in dating. I initially assumed this was just a glitch, but after almost a year of using the app with no improvement, it has become extremely frustrating. I don’t understand how CMB can be considered one of the best when the basic filtering system doesn’t consistently respect the preferences users select when creating their profiles.

Unfortunately, I’ll be deleting my account. At this point, continuing to use CMB feels more frustrating than worthwhile.

reviews.title: Not worth it
reviews.text:
I recently tried out Coffee Meets Bagel, expecting a fun and engaging dating experience, especially since I live in Salt Lake City which is a larger metro area with plenty of potential matches. Unfortunately, my experience was quite the opposite.

First off, the core premise of the app is intriguing; it connects you with potential matches based on mutual interests and preferences. However, the execution falls flat due to a significant lack of users in my area. Despite being in a sizable city, I found myself swiping through like 20 profiles and every one of them were Asian in one way or another which should have told me enough. It quickly became apparent that the app simply doesn’t have enough active real users to foster a vibrant community.

The app encourages you to add friends to help build this community, but this feature feels more like a forced gimmick than a genuine way to enhance the experience. It’s frustrating to be prompted to invite friends when the existing user base is so sparse. Instead of creating a sense of camaraderie or excitement, it highlights the app’s shortcomings and leaves you feeling isolated.

In short, Coffee Meets Bagel feels more like a ghost town than a bustling dating platform. If you’re in a larger metro area and seeking connections, you might want to look elsewhere until the app manages to attract more users. It’s a promising concept, but until they can address the user engagement issue, it’s hard to recommend it as a reliable option for datin

For instance, I will be looking at someone aged 43. If I change my search criteria to the range of 40 to 50, the person I was just looking at disappears along with everybody else.  I will be looking at somebody that lives just a few miles from me, and if I tighten up the distance range in my search criteria, that person disappears along with everybody else. Very frustrating, so I deleted my account.

reviews.title: Scam (Read before downloading)
reviews.text:
Before you download, read this: You get a certain number of people to swipe through (a batch), then you’ll be timed out until the next day. 

Here’s the upset: Those batches of people will likely NEVER be a match. The app will then tease you with people who’ve liked your profile, but you won’t have access to those people. They use “batches” to accumulate who likes who, then keep you from seeing who likes for payment. 

You will essentially  NEVER match with someone in your batch.. its main purpose is to show the person you like (and vice versa) that “someone” (you) likes them & charges them to see it. 

You will be forced to pay $109, $90 or $39/mth (the cheapest) just to see those matches. A lot of apps does this… and the only app that doesn’t so far, is the “Duet” app, which is way more transparent & you’ll actually get matches without essentially paying for a match that may or may not work out. CMB should be ashamed of this.

People should have the choice of whether or not they would like to pay a subscription and not try to be forced into it. Secondly, making people wait like three days to see if someone liked their profiles or not is ridiculous. Third of all, it’s false advertising that this app was advertised as an app where users could schedule dates only to see that that’s not even a feature on here…so overall my experience is not the best but definitely wasn’t the worst either…

reviews.title: Horrible experience
reviews.text: The concept of this app makes sense but in execution it fails horribly. Every day at noon you get access to new matches and you only get a limited number of possible matches. Sounds great until you find out regardless of if you like them or not that’s all you get as well as the number of people that are recommended to you changes. Few days ago I had several recommendations I just got off it and I only sent out one like now I have to wait a full day. This is all an attempt for you to buy their subscription plan which the cheapest one is $40 for a month. If they had a weekly plan I’d consider it but I’m not dropping that kind of money for this dumpster fire

reviews.title: more fake nonsense
reviews.text: this is just like tinder hinge bumble match etc. mostly fake profiles, &/or paid profiles (for influencers to get people to like & subscribe their social media and only fans), &/or cancelled profiles continued to be maintained by the app developers & app staff to keep people engaged on the site & generate income. i see many of the exact same profiles across all these apps & they never respond on the app nor on their social media. it's all a scam, but we know this by now right? it's a money grab. i have had numerous conversations on these apps with whoever runs the fake profiles, but never once have i been able to get anyone to meet in public. i have had numerous profiles on all apps try to get me to subscribe monthly (paid) to their only fans. i've had numerous ask me to be a sugar daddy, ha. i've had sex offered at a price on these apps many times. & all of them will have several fake profiles "like" u soon after u join but u can't see who the people are unless u start a paid subscription/membership. so much fake nonsense. all these apps are likely run by one company.

reviews.title: Getting Bagels That Violate Dealbreaker Preferences
reviews.text:
I've tried the majority of dating apps and always had the best luck with Hinge. Unfortunately, while I still get matches, the quality of conversation and dates have been lackluster. I decided to try CMB because it supposedly has a similar vibe with more long-term thinking.

I have two Dealbreaker preferences set and this is Day 3 where the majority of bagels were against my Dealbreaker preferences. What's the point of a dating app if your choices aren't adequately reflected? Definitely doesn't feel like dating with intention.

Also, I have four likes that I cannot see unless I pay... Definitely not going to pay to see potential matches if my preferences aren't being adhered to. Waste of time.

reviews.title: Used to be decent, now just a cash grab
reviews.text: I noticed my review disappeared. Allow me to rewrite - This app is awful. I am a man currently in a relationship that I found on another app. This app is Very expensive and gave me no matches. Don’t want to be rude, but the matches I got on here were clearly the “lowest tier”. I don’t know how else to say that. I think they actually have an “undesirable” bucket and if you get into that group somehow, there’s no way out. I got lots of matches with the same photos and bio on another app, which turned into a multiple meet ups and finally a relationship. This app didn’t used to be this way. I used it years ago, and after a short time I got quality matches and chats. Several per day when I was active, and it turned into a relationship over 1 year which obviously didn’t work after that. Anyway, the point is this alp is not like it used to be at all.  Time to avoid CMB like the plague

reviews.title: Worst app ever - no one here!
reviews.text:
Give 0 if I could - from what I can tell no one uses this app - most days I don’t even get suggestions and there usually isn’t anyone in discovery or if there is it’s one or two people. I’ve used apps to meet people for about 9 years now and this is the only one I’ve never actually met anyone on. Can’t even imagine why anyone would think of paying for this app!

To update based on the response from CMB - I have the app setting set same as all my other apps that I use to meet people (those other apps I’ve actually had matches on and actually met humans in person). As a male this app is a waste of space on my phone. Maybe if I were female I’d have better luck but it’s doubtful

reviews.title: Don’t waste your time
reviews.text:
Don’t waste your time or money. Do it free with WAAY more local and closer people. I paid yet still had to send “flowers” to notify the guy I “liked” him. First off…flowers? To a man? I’m a woman! Zero of the men responded or reciprocated. And since I only paid for the lower subscription, my “like” would just put my profile in the shuffle of woman the guy would see THE NEXT DAY!
I’m paying. Why can’t he be notified instantly?! And it should be that way for women regardless. The men will make a match with you and do one of two things; message you “hey” then nothing…ever! Or send you nothing. I don’t get it…they’re paying but putting in zero effort. Within 2 weeks on Facebook dating, I have 2 dates. This app? Nothing. Ghosted and ignored. And having to sift through profile after profile…it gets exhausting. And there are TONS of repeated profiles you will see again that you already passed on.

reviews.title: Run for the Hills
reviews.text: This is such a waste of time. Takes any half wit 3 seconds to realize. You think to yourself, maybe it isn’t as horrible as it seems and give it another 48 hours for mostly nothing substantial. It’s really a dry dessert for those who don’t pay. I can’t speak for those who do. I can’t justify spending money on a service who can’t provide me with a single iota of proof that there’s a chance of it providing anyone to sort through. I think I got 3 suggestions the first day. Then I had to wait like 24 hours and got 2 or 3 more, as my memory recollects. Third day one! Just one!! Haha I matched with two guys. I have about 18 that won’t pop into discovery for whatever reason, but they liked me and I can’t even see them. Biggest waste of time, truly.

reviews.title: Don’t waste your money
reviews.text: It’s free dl but nothing about it is free.  Simply put it’s monetize dating in the worst kind of way.  You have to spend money to send flowers to people you’re interested and you have to subscribe if you want to see who likes you. Here’s the problem with online dating, I spend money to buy flowers, send to people I’m interested and never hear back! So now I have no flowers and have to buy more.  In order to do simple things to view who likes you or search for someone your type, you have to subscribe and the subscription fee not cheap.  This is a predator app hunting poor souls like myself looking to meeting someone.  I’m dumping this PoS app and going back to doing things the old fashion way, meeting someone f2f.  Gluck to all who keeps paying for this and remember love is free.

reviews.title: I don’t like it
reviews.text:
Obviously my first time trying a dating app, the app has a good concept of paying $40 which would make you think that people would be serious because you HAVE TO PAY to even see who likes you and want to message you. However, it’s not the app, it’s the people! I’m sorry to say but the people are just weird as ever. Most people like you for the sake of liking you to match. When you do match they don’t message you. I even took initiative to message a few and they did not respond. The people are weird and make no sense. 

Furthermore, people with 1 face photo or no face photos should be screened and removed from the app because it’s giving creep and catfish.

The 2 stars are for the make and concept of the app. Nothing else.

reviews.title: Something Fishy
reviews.text:
I have had dates as a result of this app, but there’s something fishy going on. During slow periods I will suddenly get a like or a match, but the “person” doesn’t engage or writes like a bot. If the chat with that “person” expires and new, similar match suddenly appears. It really seems like the app creates false likes/matches to keep you using it and interested. 

Before you pay, you get lots of “likes” that are blurred. And a lot of them. Rapidly. So I paid. None of them seemed real. Then I used the app for a month as a paid member. Pace of likes slowed considerably even laying at the highest tier. So before you pay you are considerably more popular? Seems bogus. After letting my membership expire, the SAME blurred “likes” appeared rapidly to try to entice me to pay again. SAME PICTURES. Which seems impossible if I rejected them a month earlier, unless they are created by this company. 

So while there are real people on here, there are fake profiles that “like” you to push you to pay for their service, stay active and keep paying.

Go meet someone in person. That’s been so much easier and better long-term.

reviews.title: Terrible platform - even worse customer service
reviews.text: The customer service ignored my request to refund my money. I reached out with 15 min of signing up for a subscription because I knew the platform was not a fit for me. Too many Asian and East Asian members. Suggestions still fall out of my age range and preferred match suggestions that don’t align with my settings. Several fake profiles. Customer service ignored my request and just kept responding with patronizing suggestions that I had already been doing. They finally referred me to apple subcriptions to cancel which I can’t do while the purchase is pending. This platform is probably one of the worst designed dating apps I have seen. They will do everything not to honor their 7 day refund policy, Total garbage of 40 dollars, which they know, because this app is simply designed to take money of people with minimal support on this platform.

reviews.title: Waste of money. Search doesn’t work, matches don’t show up, messages disappear. Support doesn’t care
reviews.text:
I was a paid user but no longer. 
This used to be a good app, but in the last year the Search function doesn’t work, matches don’t show up, and messages have disappeared multiple times, then reappeared days or weeks later.
I have tried to help and have raised multiple tickets but support just gives me the run around, like in the last ticket asking me to “pull a HAR log” which is nonsensical as I am using their app not a webpage so I cannot create a HAR log for an app. 
Bad and just getting worse, I am never paying for this app again even if they fix the problems.

Update: 
So now they have reached out to me via email asking me to submit a new ticket, why…. So the support team can gaslight me again, or so the support team can ignore the tickets. 
Suggestion, you have my email, look up the 11 tickets that I already submitted, the same 11 tickets that your support team already closed without addressing the issues being reported. 
I cannot speak for anyone else but I am taking my wallet and never coming back.

reviews.title: What Happened?
reviews.text:
I used CMB (no paid subscription) several years ago and thought it was great, had some solid matches and several nice dates. So now that I’m back on the market, I came back thinking the experience would be similar. 

But now? Almost everything is paywalled (and WAY overpriced, even for relatively basic features), suggested matches aren’t at all my type, you can’t see most people who liked you without paying, and I’m convinced that many women on here are no longer active users (as a free user, you can’t see if someone been online recently). Feels like applying to jobs in the current market…just throwing a paper airplane into the void with a very slim chance of receiving a response. Not sure how CMB is still rated as high as it is because these reviews suggest that a lot of people have had similar experiences (survey bias notwithstanding).

I highly recommend checking out Hinge instead. They’ve really got the free-to-use model figured out, and their algorithm appears to be making suggestions based on the information in my profile and who I like…what a crazy idea, pairing people based on common interests! Notably, Hinge *requires* you to completely fill out your profile before you can start sending/receiving likes—CMB does not, hence the glut of profiles that are extremely light on any sort of meaningful details. This forces people to make judgment calls based solely on someone’s appearance, which I’d say runs totally counter to the ethos of being an app for people who want to d

reviews.title: Not a serious app for serious daters
reviews.text:
So much spam. This app will send you notifications about "deals" "sales" or other "specials" that you can't turn off. I only want to see notifications from my matches but if you have any notifications at all you get this nonsense. Most matches just end up expiring and there isn't enough of a user base and I just never saw anyone show up in the discovery section. Only the daily "recommendations", where I'd maybe say yes to 1 person every 3-4 days. Most people who send you likes never show up in the daily recommendations. Premium is just dumb. If you want to try it for a short time the shortest duration is 1 month for $40. Forty. Dollars. No way in hell am I paying that, but the app will send you notifications every day encouraging you to pay for what is essentially nothing.

I tried this for almost 3 months and never met anyone. Exchanged numbers with 2 matches but those just fizzled out. The vast majority of matches just expired after 1-2 messages. All in all, not satisfied with my experience. I've used this app years ago and it used to be good. Since then it's fallen off a cliff.

reviews.title: The worst dating app ever
reviews.text: The user experience is just bad. The app seems to compress your pictures crazily so they look very blurry even the originals are HD. The people on this app are mostly not active so you should prepare to hear nothing even you swipe frequently with a premium subscription. The app also has a ridiculous refund policy. They say that no refund will be permitted once you subscribe, but may refund you if you cancel the subscription within 7 days. I cancelled the premium membership immediately after I subscribed because the user experience is just bad as mentioned. However, the refund requests got rejected for 3 times! Come on!! Most apps have 7-day refund policy! This whole thing looks like a scam to me!

reviews.title: Terrible App
reviews.text:
Talked into using this by a friend. I guess they haven’t used it in a long time since nothing they said was good about the app is actually there. 

Got 4 likes about 2 months ago. 2 have disappeared. I assume they deleted their accounts. The other two still do not show up in suggested regardless of preferences set. I have full belief they are fake accounts at this point to try and get you to pay to see them. Other apps will usually put those who like you at the front of the stack or close to it so you can see them within a few days. This app is garbage. Also have started to notice profiles I’ve passed on showing up again. Probably why I rarely see anyone within a decent distance from me. No one wants to use it.

reviews.title: Tries to be different but is just terrible
reviews.text: CMB honestly feels like it's built to actively work against you. It did not learn at all from my likes and dislikes to improve the daily suggestions, so every batch of people it showed me at noon was a waste of time to even look through. Chances of getting a match are very low, since there is no guarantee you'll be shown to the people you like, and vice versa. I matched with a few people I used my free beans to send flowers to.... but they ended up not responding after a couple of messages and the chats expired. The only people that these weird systems may work for are subscribers that can see their incoming likes. However, the subscription options are ridiculously expensive and not even worth considering during the sales imo. CMB tries to pretend it is for intentional dating, but it just feels like a cash grab that really fails at delivering..... anything. I gave it a chance for a solid few weeks and just deleted it. Will be sticking with Hinge.

reviews.title: I would really recommend Hinge
reviews.text: Hinge is so much better than this app - at least Hinge allows you to go through the people who liked you without asking you to pay a premium. Also, Hinge won't lock you out randomly mid-conversation and ask you to wait 72 hours for them to verify your identity after I went through all the trouble of taking photos of my government issued ID and taking video selfies. Honestly I don't understand why it it would take 72 hours to verify identity - your programming should be able to match my video profile with my photos in a few seconds. This app locked me out when I was in the middle of my conversation with someone and asked me to wait 72 hours. Are you going to run a full background check on me? Unbelievable.
